newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Details of Albania accord on unity gov't, elections.
newsitem.headline: Details of Albania accord on unity gov't, elections.

text.p: The accord signed at the weekend by Albanian President Sali Berisha and 10 political parties, aimed at ending more than a month of unrest, provides for an all-party government, and new elections by June under international observation.

The accord consists of nine points worked out in two days of talks between Berisha and representatives of his Democratic Party, which hold nearly all the seats in parliament, and nine opposition groupings of both left and right.

It gives rebels a week to hand in their weapons, and asks parliament to declare an amnesty for all those implicated in the revolt. It was the collapse of five pyramid investment schemes which initially sparked the unrest. The state of emergency is to be gradually eased and phased out.

An annex to the accord asks the Socialists to take up the 10 seats they won in last May's election to the 140-member parliament. The Socialists and some other parties boycotted the assembly, alleging that the polls were unfair. Western observers supported the allegation.
Details of the accord follow.
The following 10 parties took part:
- Democratic Party (Berisha's)
- Socialist Party (biggest opposition, ex-communists)
- Republican Party (supported Berisha, then deserted him)
- Human Rights Union (represents ethnic Greek minority)
- National Front Party (extreme right)
- Social Democratic Party (centre-left, opposition)
- Democratic Alliance Party (Centre-right, opposition)
- Social Democratic Union Party (centre-left,backed Berisha)
- Monarchist Legality Movement
- Christian Democratic Party (centre-right, vague in attitude towards Berisha)
These parties agree that:
1. The Albanian parliament should decree a general amnesty for all civilians and military persons implicated in the revolt of the usury (the pyramid investment schemes).
2. A Government of National Reconciliation with representatives of all political forces in the dialogue is to be created.
3. Within one week, arms and ammunition are to be turned in by citizens in all districts of Albania.
4. Sunday March 16, 1997 is proclaimed a national day of mourning to honour all those who lost their lives during this period.
5. Parliamentary elections are to be held no later than June 1997.
6. Parliamentary elections are to be held under complete international observation.
7. The government, in cooperation with international and Albanian institutions, should take all measures to assist damaged regions as a priority.
8. The state of emergency should be gradually eased and rescinded as soon as possible.
9. The parties should continue their dialogue.
There follow signatures of Berisha and all party leaders.
Annexes
1. An invitation is appended to this agreement, addressed to the Socialist party from all other parties, to enter parliament in order to influence the situation in a positive sense.
2. The Party of the National Front agrees with this platform but considers that the government should have been called the "The Government of National Understanding."
Signed in Tirana March 9, 1997.
